## How it works

<h3>Try it</h3><ol><li>Orbit around the building and inspect roof edges, balconies and end walls.</li><li>Open Files (folder) on the left toolbar. Toggle the checkboxes beside the IFC and LAZ files to compare each source with their overlay.</li><li>Open Sections (scissors) on the left toolbar → Add clipping plane, then click a surface to inspect the relationship between model and scan.</li></ol>
<h3>Source alignment</h3><p>The pair is <code>example-no-1.ifc</code> and <code>example-no-1.laz</code> from the xeokit examples repository. The scan has 9,265,546 points, including surrounding ground and parked cars. Both files use shared local metre coordinates. The IFC bounds are approximately X 705.512–793.626 m, Y 84.995–109.509 m, Z 82.083–106.356 m, inside the scan bounds X 694.785–802.589 m, Y 78.559–114.389 m, Z 78.515–106.567 m. Rooflines, façades and balconies visually overlap without a translation, rotation or scale correction. This visual check does not certify survey accuracy or model deviations.</p>
<h3>Developer integration</h3><p>The page checks each source’s byte length and SHA-256 before passing the original Blob to <code>viewer.add(name, blob)</code>. It loads the IFC first, then the LAZ, retaining successful imports when a later download needs a retry. The SDK handles parsing, point-cloud storage, visibility, sections and navigation. Neither file declares a projected CRS, so the example adds no geographic location or map conversion. The IFC is about 30 MB and the LAZ about 91 MB.</p><p>Copy this folder and serve it over HTTP. The published SDK and remote sample downloads require internet access.</p>
